mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (measured by the 1-month change in FEDFUNDS) increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by at least 0.1% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, the resulting monetary tightening compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises simultaneously, the combined effect of deteriorating labor market conditions and monetary tightening compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.1pp and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp in the prior month
regime_hint: labor market deterioration with monetary tightening
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both UNRATE and FEDFUNDS rose by at least 0.1pp in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (defined by quarterly GDP growth above 11500 billion dollars and monthly housing starts above 1400 thousand units), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to overvaluation and rising interest rate expectations, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 > 11500 and HOUST > 1400.

mechanism_narrative: A rising employment level (measured by the 1-month change in PAYEMS) signals improving labor market conditions and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS increased by at least 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.0%, the resulting labor market tightness and reduced risk of recession lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.0.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises simultaneously, the combined effect of a weakening supply chain and monetary tightening compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1pp in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO fell by at least 0.5% and FEDFUNDS rose by at least 0.1pp in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In supply shock regimes (defined by industrial production falling below 110), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to reduced economic activity and increased inflationary pressures, leading to negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 110.
